feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. The candidate keeps the iteration 1 controller (kp 2.0, kd 0.2, base_speed 1.4, ki 0, last_direction, weights -2..2) and changes only sensor spacing, widening x from -0.02..0.02 to -0.03..0.03 at y 0.04. Iteration 1 is the best raced design (score 75.97). Its max_error stayed at 0.061 to 0.065 on every track, and it had about 2 line-loss events on the s-bend and slalom. Iteration 2 (base 1.2, kd 0.1) and iteration 3 (kp 2.5, kd 0.1) both cut progress to about 0.10 to 0.15 on the oval and s-bend, and neither moved max_error. So speed and kp were not the levers the evidence points to, and sensor geometry is the untested lever. The candidate is a clean one-variable test against the best baseline, and every field is within contract limits with five sensors matching five weights. Watch for three things in the race. First, max_error should fall toward or below 0.06 and line_loss_events on the s-bend and slalom should drop below 2. Second, progress should hold at or above iteration 1 (s-bend 0.29, oval 0.16); if it falls, the wider spacing is costing signal and the spacing should be reverted. Third, steering_oscillation was 0.23 on the s-bend at kd 0.2, so if it stays high while max_error is still near 0.06, the next step is kd 0.15 rather than more kp. Keep ki at 0 unless rms_error shows a steady offset.
requested_changes: If progress falls below iteration 1 levels (s-bend 0.29, oval 0.16) with the wider spacing, return the sensor x positions to -0.02..0.02 and instead test sensor_size 0.016 with the iteration 1 spacing, since iteration 1 gave the best progress.

If max_error stays near 0.06 and steering_oscillation on the s-bend stays above about 0.2 with the wider spacing, lower kd from 0.2 to 0.15 in one step (iteration 1 showed kd 0.2 gave oscillation of 0.23 on the s-bend), keeping kp at 2.0.

If line_loss_events on the s-bend and slalom fall below 2 while max_error drops under 0.06, keep the new spacing and try x spread at -0.04..0.04 (step 0.02) to test whether a wider spread helps further.
